headline: Asia takes the tail of Friday's AI rout while US futures bet on a softer Fed

findings.headline: Korea carries Friday's chip sell-off into Monday as Beijing leans against forced selling
findings.body: With Japan shut for Labour Thanksgiving Day, Korea became the main outlet for AI-chip selling, led by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Over the weekend China's exchanges cut the minimum margin requirement for buying shares on credit from 100% to 80%, effective 30 November, reversing January's tightening; People's Daily puts the extra borrowing capacity at about 400 billion yuan. The test this morning is whether Europe's chip names steady with US futures or follow Seoul.

findings.headline: Bessent warns the Fed against overtightening as December hike bets fade
findings.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Fed risks a policy mistake if it keeps tightening into already tighter financial conditions, and urged it to look through noisy data towards lower energy prices. That gives traders political cover to keep paring December hike bets after Friday's Treasury rally, and it is behind the bounce in gold. Wednesday's October PCE inflation and GDP release, the day before Thanksgiving, is the week's real test of that relief.

findings.headline: Mined tankers near Hormuz add risk to crude without taking barrels away
findings.body: Iran's navy says two supertankers caught fire after hitting mines in restricted waters east of the Strait of Hormuz, without naming the vessels or the damage. No export terminal was reported hit, so the disruption premium holds but does not grow, and the surplus outlook still caps rallies ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.

view: Our view: the futures bounce is positioning, not a turn, until Wednesday's inflation data confirm the Fed relief; in a Thanksgiving-thinned week Korea and Taiwan stay the cleanest read on whether the AI-chip selling has run its course.
